question: Fluoroquinolones (e.g., ciprofloxacin) remain the first-line treatment for uncomplicated enteric fever in India due to the sensitivity of most Salmonella Typhi strains.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Correct to mark this false. Fluoroquinolone resistance in Salmonella Typhi is now prevalent across India. Current first-line options are azithromycin (mild-to-moderate disease, oral) or third-generation cephalosporins (ceftriaxone IV or cefixime oral) for typhoid fever.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Actually this statement is false. Fluoroquinolone resistance in Salmonella Typhi is widespread in India. Current first-line treatment for uncomplicated enteric fever is azithromycin (for oral) or ceftriaxone/cefixime, not fluoroquinolones.
